newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klima says welcomes Italian membership in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Klima says welcomes Italian membership in EMU.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Wednesday he would welcome Italian membership in Europe's planned monetary union (EMU) if the country remained committed to economic stability.

"I am convinced that heads of governments will make a wise and fair decision (about EMU membership) in March 1998. The necessity to adhere to the stability criteria will apply to all countries equally," Klima told journalists after a meeting with his Italian counterpart Carlo Azeglio Ciampi.

"Under these conditions, the majority of Austrians will support Italian membership," he added in response to a question whether he was worried Italian membership in EMU may jeopardise the stability of the planned single currency.
The participants in Europe's planned economic and monetary monetary union (EMU) will be chosen in March 1998 on the basis of economic performance in 1997.
They will have to comply with strict criteria on public deficits and debt, inflation, interest rates and exchange rate levels to qualify for membership.
Klima added Austria attached great importance to Italian membership in the single currency, since Italy was Austria's second most important trading partner.
"It is of special importance to Austria that Italy will become a member of EMU as soon as possible," Klima said.

The Austrian minister's remarks came ten days after he said it was "not serious" if Italy joined the monetary union one or two years after its planned starting date in 1999. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
